title: What old dance bands played
summary: Old dance bands played ragtime, waltzes and reels as written; Gabriel argues older music was harder.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: How did those old time bands sound compared to the ones now? Were they about the same style or different styles? The brass band, yeah. Well, I mean the dance bands I was thinking of. Did they play mostly things from music? Did they play waltzes and everything else too? Or what did they play? They played more waltzes.

Ragtime or what? They played ragtime, they played the waltzes, they played the shallots, well the shallots died out. Yeah. But they played the waltzes, they played the reels as much. That was really good. All that kind of stuff.
Did they play them just straight the way they were written or did they sort of add something
They played the waltzes, they were written.

In fact, the old musician played more music than the younger music playing today because the music got easier. If you take the music, if they put up there the old time from the Red Book and all that, put that old stuff up there. It ain't as jazzy but you can see where the clarinet and things is doing a lot of hard work and if you give it to these fellas what you think is so hot is all that, you put them on some of that music and you see what will happen. They can't even cut it. They can't cut it, they got to practice that stuff. Practice it day and night to get that stuff. It's just like they playing Overture, like they playing Potent Pleasant or either Simaramedy. See all that stuff is hard music. It's rote that way because the man didn't have nobody listen. Now they listen at the thing, they catch it but you have to play what you see.
